_note: Media Sowaka provides. A null url means not provided yet; the app shows the card and says the file is on its way. Move videos are keyed '<stretch>/<step>' with steps counted from 1: eyes, neck, shoulders, spine, wrists, legs. Topics are the ten on Help home: edit the text here and it changes in the app on its next open. Money worries stays reflective, never advice.

topics.name: Stress & overwhelm
topics.intro: When there is a lot on your mind.
topics.article: Making sense of what’s weighing on you
topics.question: What is asking for most of your energy right now?
topics.toolBody: List what is on your mind. Choose one thing you could make smaller, share, or leave for another day.

topics.name: Burnout
topics.intro: When your energy feels stretched thin.
topics.question: What has felt especially draining lately?
topics.toolBody: Make two lists: things that take energy, and things that give a little back. Notice one change you would like to explore.

topics.name: Pressure at work
topics.intro: Deadlines, expectations, and everything in between.
topics.question: Which expectation at work feels hardest to carry?
topics.toolBody: What is happening? What is the impact on you? What would you like to ask for? Use these three questions to sketch a conversation.

topics.name: Work–life balance
topics.intro: When work keeps spilling into the rest of life.
topics.question: Where would you like a little more space between work and life?
topics.toolBody: Name one boundary you would like to explore, who needs to know about it, and what might make it easier to keep.

topics.name: New parenthood
topics.intro: Finding your way through a new chapter.
topics.article: Making room for your needs, too
topics.question: What kind of support would feel useful to you this week?
topics.toolBody: Write down the practical help, company, or time you would appreciate. Then think about who you might ask.

topics.name: Marriage & relationships
topics.intro: Newly married, finding a rhythm, or navigating change together.
topics.article: Getting to know your shared everyday
topics.question: What would you like your partner to understand about your day?
topics.toolBody: Try finishing these sentences: “Something I appreciate is…” and “Something I would like us to talk about is…”

topics.name: Family pressure
topics.intro: Your needs, their expectations, and the space between.
topics.question: Which family expectation would you like more room to question?
topics.toolBody: Write down what you want, what others are hoping for, and where you might need a clearer conversation.

topics.name: Grief & loss
topics.intro: A place to explore what loss means for you.
topics.article: There is no single story of loss
topics.question: What would you like to put into words about your loss?
topics.tool: A letter, if you feel like it
topics.toolBody: Write to a person, a part of your life, or yourself. There is no need to finish it, share it, or make it positive.

topics.name: Money worries
topics.intro: Space to talk about the pressure money can bring.
topics.question: What about money feels most uncertain right now?
topics.tool: Separate the worry from the next step
topics.toolBody: Describe what is worrying you, what information you are missing, and one question you would like help answering.

topics.name: Life changes
topics.intro: When things are shifting around you.
topics.article: Finding your footing in a transition
topics.question: What is changing, and what would you like to hold on to?
topics.toolBody: List what is changing and what feels steady. Choose one familiar thing you would like to make room for.

affirmations.title: You don’t have to do it all
